decision.expected_measurable_effect: Reach: terminal tip position error should remain at or below the recorded 0.01 m tolerance (baseline 0.0076 m); any increase past tolerance is an adverse result and would be reported as reach degradation. Holding position: the six sampled 0.30–0.35 s tip position errors should not grow and ideally all fall inside the 0.01 m limit (baseline range 0.00764–0.05814 m). Holding speed: the six sampled holding-window tip speeds should fall toward or below the 0.02 m/s limit (baseline 0.635–1.581 m/s); a consistent reduction that still stays above the limit counts only as directionally consistent, not as a passed criterion. Computation: mean update duration, deadline_misses and per-update optimization solve time should be compared with the baseline records (mean update about 17.26 s against a 0.01 s control period, 35 of 35 deadline misses, and solver-status counts of 1 success versus 34 user-requested stops at the 15 s feasible-return budget); because nearly all solves terminated on that budget rather than on convergence, I expect wall time to stay budget-limited rather than scale with the added cost, but an increase in update wall time, deadline misses, unusable updates, or constraint violation would be a measurable adverse effect. Full historical warm plans and optimizer iteration traces are not retained, so per-iteration cost attribution cannot be checked.
decision.rationale: Accepted diagnosis (possible, bounded): the failing sampled criterion includes holding-window tip speed — across all six recorded rows of the 0.30–0.35 s window every sampled tip speed exceeds the 0.02 m/s limit (0.635–1.581 m/s), while the smallest sampled position error (0.00764 m) is inside the 0.01 m limit and the largest (0.05814 m) is not; terminal reach passes at 0.0076 m against the 0.01 m tolerance. The saved recipe shows holding_tip_speed_weight = 0.0, so the holding window currently carries no tip-speed cost at all. Hypothesis: the settling failure includes residual tip speed inside the settling window, and adding a nonzero per-second squared spatial tip-speed cost at nodes at/after the window start makes the optimizer prefer settling-window trajectories that are slower at the tip, which is directly the criterion that fails. Weight relevance: holding_tip_speed_weight is defined on exactly those nodes, and explicit settling settings are present (settling window 0.05 s with position limit 0.01 m and speed limit 0.02 m/s), satisfying the parameter's requirement. I select the holding weight alone rather than also changing terminal_tip_speed_weight: terminal reach already passes, the terminal instant lies inside the penalized holding window anyway, and changing both at once would confound the one model-selected complete experiment the grant allows. Value 0.01: clearly effective (above the 0.0001 minimum for a new positive selection) and well below the 1.0 bound, deliberately modest relative to the configured terminal_weight so that a directional effect can be seen without saturating the trade-off, leaving room for a later bounded increase if the effect is right but too small. Coverage and limits: this rests on six holding rows plus batched endpoint samples and run-level scalars, not a trajectory-wide characterization; trajectory-wide holding co-variation was not displayed; the diagnosis rates the residual-tip-motion explanation only 'possible' and the one-step-projection explanation 'insufficient_evidence'; no closed-loop counterfactual replay or causal attribution capability exists, so this is a bounded test of a stated hypothesis, not an adoption of a proven cause. Observations that would weaken the hypothesis: unchanged or higher holding-window tip speeds; new or larger holding position errors; terminal error leaving the 0.01 m tolerance; sampled holding speed falling only for one row while others stay far above the limit; or a material rise in update wall time, deadline misses or unusable updates. Local comparison deliberately omitted: the grant requires a legal saved baseline update with effective horizon 0.01 s, and no such update is identified in the displayed evidence (cataloged per-update effective horizons are 5, 7 and 10 control intervals at a 0.01 s control period), so no legal paired state can be nominated.
